notes: Hand-authored, unlike data/skills.json — edit this file directly, nothing regenerates it.

A coach can retune the whole app from here: change a prescription to change every session at that level, add a template to add a split, or rewrite the block structure to change how a session is ordered.
block.include picks the pool: 'working' = unlocked but not yet cleared (what you are chasing), 'owned' = already cleared (what you train for volume), 'any' = both.

Skills are never named here. Blocks describe WHAT to pick (hold vs reps, which branches, which tier relative to the athlete) and js/coach.js resolves that against whatever the athlete has actually unlocked.
General programming, not individual coaching. It knows nothing about injuries, sleep or recovery.

Thai copy: focus.labelTh and block.labelTh/noteTh are used when the interface is in Thai. Templates take optional nameTh and summaryTh the same way — add them and they are picked up automatically; without them the English text is shown.

blocks.label: Skill work
blocks.note: First, on a fresh nervous system. Quality over accumulation — end the set while the shape is still clean.
blocks.noteTh: ทำเป็นอย่างแรกตอนที่ระบบประสาทยังสด เน้นคุณภาพมากกว่าปริมาณ — หยุดเซ็ตตอนที่ฟอร์มยังสวย

blocks.label: Strength
blocks.note: The session's main work. Full range, controlled negative, stop 1–2 reps short of failure.
blocks.noteTh: งานหลักของวัน เต็มช่วงการเคลื่อนไหว ลงช้าและควบคุม หยุดก่อนหมดแรง 1–2 ครั้ง

blocks.label: Accessory
blocks.note: Skills you already own, a tier below your working level. Volume and joint prep — this is where the reps live, not where you chase a new shape.
blocks.noteTh: ท่าที่คุณผ่านแล้ว ต่ำกว่าระดับที่ฝึกอยู่หนึ่งขั้น เน้นปริมาณและเตรียมข้อต่อ ไม่ใช่การไล่ท่าใหม่

templates.name: Foundation full-body
templates.summary: Three full-body days with a rest day between each. Everything is trained often enough to learn the movement, lightly enough to recover.

templates.name: Upper / lower
templates.summary: Four days, upper and lower alternating. Slightly more volume per movement than the full-body split once three days stops being enough.

templates.name: Push / pull split
templates.summary: The standard intermediate split. Push and pull get a dedicated day each, with a skill day for handstand and ring work.

templates.name: Push / pull / legs
templates.summary: Five days. Each pattern twice a fortnight with a core day — for when four days is recovering easily.

templates.name: Straight-arm focus
templates.summary: Static work leads every session and dynamic strength follows it. This is the split for planche and front-lever progress.

templates.name: Rings emphasis
templates.summary: Ring strength twice a week either side of the push and pull days, for the cross and ring-planche line.

templates.name: High-frequency skill
templates.summary: Six short sessions. At this level the limit is connective tissue, not muscle — frequent low-volume exposure beats long sessions.
